events.label: FOMC meeting opens (Jul 28-29) — Chair Warsh; September hike 82% per FedWatch; Brent $89.73 changes calculus
events.note: Updated as of July 27 morning: FOMC meets July 28-29 with Chair Kevin Warsh presiding (decision 2pm ET July 29, press conference 2:30pm ET). July rate hike probability ~35%; July hold remains modal. September hike probability 82% per CME FedWatch as of Monday morning (tool lagging the real-time Brent retreat — directional reprice toward 65-70% expected intraday as Brent-sub-$90 deflates inflation expectations). US-Iran mutual pause sent Brent -7.3% to $89.73 and WTI -6.5% to $83.47 entering the meeting window — the most important macro input change since the July 24 Pakistan-China diplomacy signal. The FOMC Brent-above-$100 input risk is eliminated; base case is now dovish hold with September acknowledged as contingent (not the prior tightening-bias reintroduction tail). Formal breach clearance still requires Brent below $85 and September hike prob below 70% — neither confirmed. Warsh's July 29 press conference remains the year's most market-moving single event: if he explicitly closes September (probability below 55%), the upgrade clock could complete within 48 hours. If he acknowledges September as live with Brent at $89 (still above formal trigger), the relief rally stalls and SPX tests 7,380-7,400.

Tariffs on 99.4% of imports will be the first question on the AMZN call given its freight/logistics exposure. If AAPL China beats AND AMZN AWS confirms +30%+ AI demand growth AND Q2 GDP is above 2%: the briefing series' upgrade clock, if started July 27-28, could complete by Friday.

events.label: July CPI (est.) — Brent oil shock + Trump tariffs on 99.4% of imports; dual inflation embedding, reduced by Iran pause
events.note: Updated as of July 27 morning: Two major inflation inputs, with the first partially moderated by the Iran mutual pause. (1) Brent crude: averaged ~$97-100 for multiple sessions before the July 27 US-Iran pause sent Brent to $89.73. Gasoline follows Brent with a 2-3 week lag — the $97-100 period (roughly July 14-24) is already embedded in the gasoline component of August CPI; the post-pause retreat ($89-90) will partially offset but cannot fully reverse the embedded pass-through. Net CPI oil contribution: materially positive but not the worst-case $100+ ceiling scenario. (2) Trump's 10-12.5% tariffs on 99.4% of US imports (effective July 24) remain the second inflationary input, adding import cost pressure across consumer goods, autos, and industrial inputs. September cumulative hike probability: 82% per CME FedWatch as of July 27 morning (lagging oil retreat; likely repricing toward 65-70% intraday). A July CPI print above 3.5% YoY (oil $97-100 peak + tariff pass-through; moderated but not negated by the Iran pause) still makes September near-certain. Bull scenario (CPI ≤3.0%): oil-pass-through didn't fully embed in core by August 13; September probability falls below 50%. Bear scenario (CPI ≥3.8%): dual oil+tariff pass-through exceeds expectations; September 50bps probability above 90%, BEARISH regime re-activated.
